current_verified_vs_unchecked: VERIFIED: OpenCL residual MLP execution on NVIDIA/AMD pair (host-staged, shared memory).
VERIFIED: Pure planner capacity logic and refusal states.
UNCHECKED: Four physical discrete cards (not present).
UNCHECKED: Dedicated VRAM allocation and P2P transfers.

tests.setup: Invoke executor with --device-ids <A> <B> <C> <D>. Ensure A-D map to four unique physical PCI IDs. Attempt a run where two aliases resolve to the same physical GPU ID.
tests.negative_discriminator: Executor must reject duplicate physical IDs before native allocation or context creation.
tests.expected_observation: Exit code 2 (REFUSED) with error 'Duplicate physical device'. No GPU kernels launched.
tests.required_evidence: JSON receipt showing 'status': 'REJECTED' and zero kernel events recorded.

tests.setup: Run standard 4-device MLP fixture (width 512, layers 16). Inspect per-device logs for weight hashes and layer indices.
tests.negative_discriminator: Detects whole-model replication or CPU offload fallback which would show identical weights on multiple devices or missing GPU kernel counts.
tests.expected_observation: Each of the 4 devices reports exactly 4 unique layer ownerships. Total unique weights = 16. No device reports 'CPU_fallback' or duplicate weight hashes.
tests.required_evidence: Per-device JSON blocks containing distinct 'assigned_layer_ids' and matching 'weight_hash' entries.

tests.setup: Configure policy-mib such that total modeled budget for 3 cards is insufficient for the 16-layer workload (e.g., force 3-device mode with tight caps), while 4-device mode fits.
tests.negative_discriminator: Planner or Executor must refuse allocation if aggregate budget < required block size, rather than silently offloading to CPU or crashing.
tests.expected_observation: Exit code 2 (REFUSED) with message indicating 'Total block memory exceeds usable aggregate budget' or similar capacity failure.
tests.required_evidence: Receipt showing attempted allocation bytes vs available budget per device.

tests.setup: Execute 4-device run with --inject-corruption flag targeting the activation buffer at the boundary between Device B and Device C.
tests.negative_discriminator: Ensures corruption propagates through subsequent layers (C and D) and fails final parity check against independent CPU reference.
tests.expected_observation: Devices A and B complete successfully. Device C executes corrupted input. Final output mismatch detected. Exit code 1 (FAIL).
tests.required_evidence: Log showing 'corruption_detected_at_boundary' and final tensor comparison failure.

tests.setup: Monitor actual VRAM usage via driver API (nvidia-smi/rocm-smi/intel_gpu_top) during T2 execution. Compare advertised free memory vs peak allocated memory.
tests.negative_discriminator: Prevents false PASS based on stale 'free' memory readings or host-shared memory being counted as dedicated VRAM.
tests.expected_observation: Peak VRAM usage matches expected weight+activation footprint. Advertised free memory decreases by measured amount. AMD integrated memory explicitly labeled 'shared_host_memory' and excluded from dedicated VRAM totals.
tests.required_evidence: Snapshot of driver memory stats before/during/after execution.

release_gates: Four unique physical GPUs discovered and mapped without alias duplication.
All 16 layers assigned uniquely across 4 devices with no CPU offload in GPU path.
Capacity refusal verified when using only 3 devices under constrained policy.
Corruption injection causes measurable numerical divergence and FAIL exit.
Actual dedicated VRAM allocation confirmed via driver telemetry, excluding shared host memory.
unsupported_claims: No claim of direct P2P peer-to-peer DMA transfer; all cross-device data is host-staged.
No claim of larger-than-one-card LLM inference capability; this test uses small MLP fixture.
No claim of thermal stability or electrical safety; hardware not present.
No claim of durable session recovery or worker restart resilience.
No claim of performance benefit over single-card execution; correctness only.
